hints: Both functions are the same shape: compare with root->key and go into ONE subtree. Searching both sides means you have written a binary-tree search, not a BST search.
insertKey returns the root so the caller can reattach it: root->left = insertKey(root->left, key). Forgetting the assignment builds a tree that silently loses every node.
The empty-tree case is where the new node is actually created - that is the base case of the recursion, not a special case before it.
source: DSA Lab Week 2 ADT: insert(T,k) and search(T,k)
title: BST insert and search
